title: L Antigen Family Member 3 stabilizes stalled replication forks by reducing MRE11 resection to maintain genome stability.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the Europe PMC supplement (48 MB): it is one 47 MB PDF plus the seven main figure images, nothing else. Extracted 812,117 characters of text from that PDF with a Python decompressor: it contains only figure panel labels and axis numbers, and the strings 'Supplementary Table' and 'Table S' appear zero times. Read the ProteomeXchange record for PXD066518: it lists exactly 8 files (4 Thermo .raw, 4 Proteome Discoverer .msf) hosted at iProX. HEAD requests confirmed they are live and public but large (LAGE3-S.raw = 650 MB, LAGE3-S.msf = 171 MB). PRIDE's own API returns 404 because the deposit is hosted at iProX, not PRIDE.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The biology (LAGE3 and the other KEOPS complex subunits sit at stalled replication forks and limit the MRE11 nuclease from chewing back newly made DNA), the experimental design, and the claim that 'the data underlying this article are available in the article and in its Supplementary material'. All per-cell and per-DNA-fibre measurements behind the figures were read only as plotted points, never as numbers in a file.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplement downloads freely; the proteomics deposit PXD066518 is public at iProX and HEAD returned HTTP 200 for both file types. No login or access application. Passes, but what downloads is raw mass spectrometry, not a table.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified in the files. There is no data table anywhere: the supplement is a single PDF of figure images and the deposit holds only raw instrument files. Every quantity the paper reports (IdU/CldU fibre-length ratios, gamma-H2AX foci counts, comet tail moments, chromosome aberrations) exists only as dots on a plot, so any prediction target would have to be constructed from scratch by digitising figures or by re-searching the raw spectra.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. No feature matrix exists. The only machine-readable inputs are 4 .raw spectrum files; the proteins they identify are not listed in any released file, so even the TurboID (proximity-labelling) hit list would have to be regenerated with a search engine.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable in the sense required: axis labels in the figures carry units (micrometres for fibre tracts, percentages, OD450) but there is no units column because there is no column.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, verified. The entire machine-readable dataset is 4 mass spectrometry runs (GFP control and LAGE3-TurboID, each with and without hydroxyurea), with no biological replicates. Far under the ~1,500-row or even ~400-row floor.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~3.3 GB of Thermo .raw plus ~0.7 GB of .msf
a6_fits_laptop.note: FAIL on policy and size. Individual files are 171-650 MB, over the 50 MB cap, and the project rules forbid downloading raw mass spectrometry at all. Re-searching .raw files also needs Windows-only or heavyweight tooling.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be assessed: the paper states no row or protein counts for a deposited table, and no table was deposited, so there is nothing to reconcile.

a8_label_provenance.note: Cannot be traced. Any candidate label (for example 'is a stalled-fork protector') would have to be defined by the evaluator from figure panels or from a re-run database search, which is label construction, not a measured column.

existing_models.name: DNAi, an open-source deep-learning tool that measures DNA fibre tracts in microscope images (Nucleic Acids Research 2026, gkag335)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors as trained on a diverse image collection spanning nascent-DNA-stability, fork-protection and S1-nuclease experiments; exact held-out metrics not retrieved, only the abstract-level description.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Unbiased, operator-independent fibre measurement across labs and imaging setups; not retrieved in detail.

existing_models.name: FiberAI, a deep-learning detector for nascent DNA fibres in high-throughput microscopy (bioRxiv 2020)
existing_models.score_and_split: Described as detecting and quantifying fibres in high-throughput images; no number retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Manual fibre quantification is laborious; throughput was the stated problem.

existing_models.name: qAID, a quantitative AI-based DNA fibre workflow (bioRxiv 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Authors report it measures fibre class frequencies, fork speed and fork symmetry, including nascent-DNA degradation in homologous-recombination-deficient cells; no held-out number retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Subtle fork-symmetry variation and degradation phenotypes; not retrieved in detail.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the natural backbone for a fork-protein classifier
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for embeddings, but there is no label set to fit a head on
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; irrelevant here because no training data exists

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. BioGRID or IntAct (protein interaction databases) and UniProt could in principle be joined on gene symbol or UniProt accession, but this paper releases no protein list to join.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could not be written from this paper's released data, because no identifier list is released.

controls.positive_control: The paper's own biology offers obvious ones (MRE11, BRCA2 and SMARCAL1 are textbook fork-protection factors a model should rank highly), but no dataset exists to run them on.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is not applicable: there are no labels.
controls.external_validation: None available from this paper; BioGRID or the ProHits-viz BioID contaminant repository would be the external sources if a protein list existed.

honest_claim_h3: No model claim is possible from the released data: the paper publishes a mechanistic cell-biology story whose numbers live only inside figure images, plus four unreplicated raw mass spectrometry runs.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence and interaction context to predict which proteins protect stalled DNA copying machinery from being chewed back.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would have trained on a list of proteins labelled as present or absent at stalled replication forks, taken from the paper's proximity-labelling screen. That list is not released; the only machine-readable items are 4 mass spectrometry runs.
plain_idea.predict: A yes/no score for whether a protein acts as a stalled-fork protector. The true answer would have come from the DNA fibre assay, in which newly made DNA is labelled with two nucleoside analogues and the shortening of the second label after hydroxyurea treatment is measured under a microscope.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: DNA-repair labs studying Galloway-Mowat syndrome and replication stress would use a ranked candidate list to pick which genes to knock down next; even a failed model would say whether sequence alone carries any signal about fork protection.

more_or_better_data.why: The existing tools (DNAi, FiberAI, qAID) were trained on large collections of DNA fibre microscopy images; this paper releases no images and no measurements, only 4 raw mass spectrometry files.

confidence_score.why: With one sample per condition and no replicates in the deposit, nothing supports estimating measurement noise or per-prediction confidence.

models_beatable.why: DNAi is a 2026 open tool and qAID a 2025 one, both purpose-built for exactly the image analysis this assay needs; with no images released here there is nothing to compete on.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails every condition: we cannot run their model (no images), we see strictly less data than they did, and there is no shared evaluation split.

ml_idea: The only idea the paper suggests is ranking proteins by likelihood of acting at stalled replication forks, trained on the LAGE3 TurboID proximity-labelling hits. It dies immediately: the hit list is not deposited, only 4 raw spectrum files are, and a 4-run screen with no replicates cannot supply labels for any model.

effort.compute_note: Working set is the sum of the 8 deposited files inferred from HEAD requests (650 MB and 171 MB measured for two of them, the rest assumed similar). No training compute estimated because no trainable dataset exists.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Unzip the supplement and grep it for 'Table': it is a single PDF of figure images with zero supplementary tables, which kills the project in two minutes.

verdict_reason: Verified in the files: no data table exists anywhere. The 48 MB supplement is one PDF of figure images with no supplementary tables, and the public deposit PXD066518 holds only 4 unreplicated raw mass spectrometry runs (650 MB each) plus their search-engine binaries. Fails A2 (the label would have to be built by digitising figures or re-searching spectra), A3 (no inputs released), A5 (4 machine-readable items), and A6 (raw mass spectrometry, over the size cap and against policy). A good mechanistic paper, but there is nothing here to model.
